title: Select Sector indices — conditional quarter-end secondary reweighting (24%/4.8%/50% breach test) — the year-end instance
source: EST: rule-derived, not a scheduled publication. SEC EDGAR, Select Sector SPDR Trust Form 497, accession 0001193125-26-031948, document d85739d497.htm, RE-FETCHED DIRECT 2026-09-08 by this event's own initial research (HTTP 200, 2,388,335 bytes — byte-identical to the 2026-09-05 sibling fetch) rather than inherited from the proposal that filed it: 'if, on the second to last business day of March, June, September, or December a company has a weight greater than 24% or the sum of the companies with weights greater than 4.8% exceeds 50%, a secondary reweighting will be triggered with the reweighting effective date being after the close of the last business day of the month.' The same filing dates the quarterly reset that precedes it: 'The rebalancing of the Select Sector Indices … occurs at the closing prices of the second Friday of March, June, September and December. Changes will become effective after the market close on the third Friday.' December 2026 weekday arithmetic, computed mechanically: second Friday 2026-12-11 (reference close), third Friday 2026-12-18 (capping effective after the close), last business day Thu 2026-12-31 (Christmas Day 12-25 is a Friday closure and New Year's Day 2027-01-01 is the next), second-to-last business day Wed 2026-12-30 (the test). So the test is 12-30 and the trade, IF triggered, clears after the 12-31 close. Filed estimate because the trigger is CONDITIONAL — no primary source can pre-confirm a breach, so this entry can never be promoted to confirmed before the fact; the date itself is not in doubt
notes: A BACKSTOP, not a base case — the year-end analogue of sp-select-sector-secondary-reweight-2026-09-30 and -2027-03-31, and the fourth quarter of a sequence this calendar tracked for three quarters with the year-end one missing. Canonical file written 2026-09-08 by this event's own never-assessed initial research, which read the single proposal that filed it (proposals/sp-select-sector-secondary-reweight-2026-12-31.from-russell-style-quarter-end-capping-effective-2026-09-30.json) and did the two things that proposal explicitly asked for and had not done: re-fetched the Form 497 directly rather than inheriting the quote, and re-ran the breach arithmetic under the live capping rule. WHAT THAT RESEARCH ADDS THAT THE SIBLINGS DO NOT HAVE: the December reset-to-test window has never once produced the move the single-name leg needs. Over eleven consecutive Decembers (2015-2025), AMZN's relative return versus XLY from the third-Friday close to the second-to-last December session peaked at +3.34% against the +4.35% a 23.00% capped weight needs to re-cross 24.00% — 0 of 11. The mechanism is measured, not assumed: AMZN-vs-XLY daily excess-return stdev across 12-21..12-31 runs at 1.065% against 1.393% all-period (76.5%), and seasonally-conditioned seven-session windows re-breach at 8.4% against the 10.3% unconditional rate the 2027-03-31 sibling established. Second finding, a correction to that sibling's four-quarter table: December's window is seven SESSIONS but ~6.5 trading days, because Christmas Eve 2026-12-24 is a 1:00 p.m. ET half close (christmas-eve-half-day-2026-12-24) — December is the one quarter where session count overstates trading hours. Impact low and symbols EMPTY to match all three siblings; kind sector matches them too, and the imperfect enum fit for a market-structure flow event is named rather than fixed from this lane. Full workup, eleven-fund baseline screen and both registered forward tests: docs/research/events/sp-select-sector-secondary-reweight-2026-12-31.md.
